incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act (the 'Company Act') Articles 128, 129, 154, 156, 172, 178, 192, 193, 202, 208, 410, 435; Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals Articles 7 and 12.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Investment Commission (IC-MOEA) for foreign investment approval; Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce for company incorporation registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation Registration and Articles of Incorporation (Company Establishment Registration) submitted through the MOEA one-stop company registration system.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Taiwan's Company Act does not prescribe a minimum paid-up capital for limited liability companies. The subscribers determine the paid-up capital and deposit it into a temporary company bank account; a certified public accountant must issue a capital verification report. No escrow or blocked account is required, provided funds are fully paid before registration and the capital plan is consistent with the Foreign Investment Approval.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
IN THE MATTER OF THE INCORPORATION AND INITIAL GOVERNANCE OF [COMPANY ENGLISH NAME] LIMITED (the 'Company')

RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS

Adopted in writing this ____ day of ______, 20__, at ____________, Taiwan (R.O.C.).

The Board of Directors of the Company met, and the following directors were present in person or by electronic means: ____________________ (Chairperson), ____________________, and ____________________. The directors present constituted a quorum under Articles 202 and 206 of the Taiwan Company Act. The chairperson noted that all subscribers had executed the Articles of Incorporation, the Foreign Investment Approval Letter had been obtained from the Investment Commission of the Ministry of Economic Affairs, and the full subscribed capital had been deposited in the Company's temporary capital account.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED THAT:

1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION. The subscribed share capital of the Company is [currency] ________, divided into _______ shares of par value ________ each. All shares have been fully subscribed and paid as required. The Board approves the issuance of share certificates and directs the secretary to record the shareholders in the register of members and file the capital verification report.

2. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION. The registered office of the Company shall be established at _______________, Taiwan, as set out in the Articles of Incorporation. Management is directed to execute the lease or consent and to post the Company's name plate at that address.

3. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The Company shall open and maintain accounts with ____________ Bank. The Chairperson, General Manager, and __________ are each severally authorized to sign and execute account opening forms, operating instructions, payment orders, investment agreements, and any banking compliance declarations. Any two authorized signatories, or such other threshold as the finance policy may later specify, shall execute payments above the authorized limit.

4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. The Board appoints _____________ as Chairperson and _____________ as General Manager, and adopts the necessary corporate governance policies. The Chairperson and General Manager jointly are authorized to execute all incorporation filings, statutory declarations, tax registrations, licensing applications, and contracts with Apple Distribution International and Google LLC for digital Webtoon syndication.

5. RATIFICATION AND EFFECTIVE DATE. All prior acts taken by the incorporators and subscribers are hereby ratified. This resolution is effective immediately upon adoption, and the secretary is directed to place the original resolution in the corporate records and provide certified copies to banks, tax authorities, and regulatory bodies as required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name and Business Scope Pre-Clearing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce — Online Company Name and Business Scope Pre-Query System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit proposed Chinese and English company names through the MOEA pre-query system, specifying the intended business scope as digital webtoon publishing, comic/webtoon syndication, licensing, and related digital content services. The system screens against conflicting registrations and reserved names. The applicant should then fix the exact company name and operating scope in the Articles of Incorporation. If the foreign investor is a People's Republic of China entity, add an explicit investment-scheme disclosure to the pre-clearance file for the Investment Commission later. Any name conflict requires amendment before proceeding.
required_dossiers: Proposed Chinese and English company names
Intended business scope narrative with ISIC and MOEA code mapping
Identity certificate of the applicant or investor
Principal place of business address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name query is rejected due to resemblance, submit a revised name through the same system. If the business scope is considered ambiguous, narrow the scope to digital content creation, licensing, and distribution and resubmit before the statutory period lapses.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Approval and Fund Remittance Authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (IC-MOEA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and file Form A1 and attachments through the IC-MOEA online application. Include the board resolution, investment plan, source of funds, Articles of Incorporation, and audited financial statements of the foreign investor. The IC-MOEA reviews sectors and ownership; since digital webtoon publishing falls within permitted general industries, no special negative-list approval is needed. It will issue a Foreign Investment Approval Letter. After approval, open a foreign capital account at a domestic bank and remit share capital. China-source investment must be declared under the special cross-strait investment regulations and may require additional review before approval.
required_dossiers: Form A1 application for foreign investment approval
Power of Attorney executed by the foreign investor
Certified copy of the foreign investor registration certificate
Audited financial statements for the most recent year
Projected business plan and capital utilization schedule
Draft Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If IC-MOEA issues a query or requests supplemental materials, provide amendments before the suspension deadline. If the project is deemed restricted, propose an ownership or financing restructuring, or apply for a case-specific administrative interpretation and re-submit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce — Company Registration Section via one-stop electronic registration portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After approval, open a temporary regulated bank account under the company name, deposit the full subscribed capital, and obtain a deposit certificate. Engage a Taiwan certified public accountant to audit the capital and issue a capital verification report. File incorporation registration with MOEA, attaching the foreign investment approval, Articles of Incorporation, directors' consent declarations, registered office proof, and CPA capital verification. MOEA will issue the company registration certificate, which is conclusive proof of legal personality. Then complete seal-cutting and set up company books immediately.
required_dossiers: IC-MOEA Foreign Investment Approval Letter
Articles of Incorporation duly signed by all subscribers
Bank deposit certificate and CPA capital verification report
Consent declarations of directors and statutory officers
Registered office consent or lease agreement
Application for company incorporation registration
Power of Attorney and passport or ID of applicant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MOEA queries, cure the filing by submitting amended documents or revised Articles within the statutory response period. If the registration is rejected due to incomplete capital, coordinate with the bank and CPA to re-verify and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Tax Registration, VAT Invoice Approval and Labor Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau of the Ministry of Finance (regional office); Bureau of Labor Insurance; National Health Insurance Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, file business registration with the competent tax bureau within the prescribed period to establish the tax record. Apply for VAT uniform invoices and tax seal. Register the company as an employer with the Bureau of Labor Insurance and the National Health Insurance Administration, enrolling employees and statutory labor pension. For webtoon sales through Apple IAP and Google Play Billing, ensure proper accounting for digital content, cross-border transaction reporting, and issuance of e-receipts or B2B invoices as applicable. Maintain employment contracts and remuneration records. No industry license is required for ISIC 9000.
required_dossiers: Company registration certificate
Uniform invoice registration application form
Company seal and responsible person's seal
Lease agreement for place of business
Employee roster and labor and health insurance enrollment forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax bureau postpones VAT invoice issuance due to missing documents, supply revised tenancy proof and identity documents. If the labor bureau reports data anomalies, correct payroll records and resubmit within the cure period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Activation, Authorized Signatory Setup and Digital Payment Merchant Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Taiwan commercial bank chosen by the Company; Ministry of Economic Affairs trade licensing system (only if physical goods later added)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the company seal, responsible person's seal, and contract seals from a licensed seal cutter. Use the company registration certificate and tax ID number to open operating bank accounts and digital payment merchant accounts for Apple IAP and Google Play Billing. Pass AML-relevant beneficial ownership disclosure and sign a corporate resolution specifying signatories. If importing or exporting physical goods is ever added, apply for importer/exporter registration with MOEA; for pure digital online publishing, trade registration is not applicable. Arrange for accountants to establish books, statutory audits, and the filing calendar.
required_dossiers: Company registration certificate and Articles of Incorporation
Board resolution for bank account authorizations and signatories
Foreign Investment Approval Letter for the bank file
Beneficial ownership declaration forms
Tax ID certificate and tax clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank compliance team declines due to missing economic substance evidence, submit webtoon platform contracts, licensing agreements, and projected revenue flows. If a signature specimen is mismatched, re-execute the board resolution and notarize as required.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable — No industrial licensing authority applies to ISIC 9000 digital webtoon publishing and syndication.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable — General business registration with the National Taxation Bureau and company incorporation registration with MOEA are sufficient for pure digital publishing.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable — Taiwan Environmental Protection Administration would be the counterparty only if an EIA-triggering physical project were added.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable — ISIC 9000 online publishing does not fall under any of the EIA categories of Article 4 of the Taiwan Environmental Impact Assessment Act; the activity is exempt from environmental impact assessment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable — no stationary emission source, no wastewater discharge point, no VOC-emitting process, and no hazardous waste generation above office de minimis levels; e-waste must be handled by registered recyclers if generated.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable as a Civil Defense fire permit for manufacturing. However, the office premises must comply with the Taiwan Fire Services Act, including fire extinguishers, escape route signage, and building occupancy safety. General workplace safety requirements under the Occupational Safety and Health Act apply. If a small creative studio is included, the local building management office may require an interior decoration or building-use inspection, but no Civil Defense manufacturing license is required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China; electronic portal: the STA's official online tax service platform accessible via the China Electronic Tax Administration (e-Tax) system at https://tpass.etax.chinatax.gov.cn and provincial-level e-Tax portals for foreign-invested enterprises.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident investor establishing a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE) in the People's Republic of China, the statutory Tax Identification Number (TIN) is the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), which also serves as the taxpayer identification number. The procurement procedure is: (1) complete the establishment registration with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through the enterprise registration online platform to obtain the USCC; (2) within 30 days of the issuance of the business license, complete tax registration with the competent local tax authority (a branch of the State Taxation Administration) through the electronic tax bureau or in-person service hall, submitting the investor's passport or equivalent identity documents, certificate of incorporation, board resolutions, articles of association, registered address proof, and lease agreement for the registered Chinese business premises; (3) upon completion, the tax authority issues the taxpayer registration certificate and activates the enterprise's e-tax account; (4) the WFOE must thereafter use the USCC for all VAT CIT withholding and reporting obligations. No minimum registered capital is required for the tax registration itself, but foreign exchange capital injection rules under the Foreign Investment Law and SAFE circulars must be observed.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None: China does not operate a check-the-box pass-through election regime for foreign-owned limited liability companies. The WFOE is a resident enterprise taxed on its worldwide income at entity level under the Corporate Income Tax Law. No hybrid mismatch election is available domestically; hybrid mismatch outcomes are addressed only through the general anti-avoidance rules and the OECD multilateral instrument positions adopted by China.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For the digital webtoon publishing and electronic content distribution services rendered by a WFOE, the mandatory VAT registration threshold is effectively zero: enterprises are required to register for VAT regardless of turnover because a limited liability company must issue special VAT invoices and is considered a VAT general taxpayer under the Measures for the Administration of VAT Registration. For small-scale taxpayers the annual sales threshold is RMB 5 million; however a newly established WFOE typically applies for general taxpayer status immediately to facilitate input VAT credits and export zero-rating claims. The statutory threshold for small-scale taxpayers is RMB 5,000,000 in annual taxable sales.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China mandates the use of the State Taxation Administration's fully digitalized electronic invoice (e-invoice) system for general VAT taxpayers, with real-time fiscal clearance through the e-Tax platform and the nationwide Electronic Invoice Service Platform. Enterprises are required to adopt the 'fully digitalized electronic invoice' (shuzi dianzi fapiao) regime in the pilot expansion areas and must issue VAT invoices through the STA-authorized tax control system or the newly mandated digital e-invoice system. The system uses cryptographic digital signatures, enterprise digital credentials, and real-time upload of invoice metadata to the STA's central systems for anti-fraud matching. There is no physical fiscal stamping; the nationwide platform conducts automated cross-verification against VAT returns, customs declarations, and export documentation. For cross-border transactions, the electronic port authority (China International Trade Single Window) interoperates with the VAT system to reconcile export invoices and customs declarations.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to the export of goods and to qualifying offshore services provided to overseas parties under China's VAT zero-rating and VAT exemption-with-credit policies for cross-border services. A Chinese WFOE in the digital content business can claim zero-rating for services rendered to overseas customers, including digital publishing and syndication of copyrighted webtoon content, where: (1) the service recipient is domiciled outside China; (2) the services are consumed outside China; (3) the consideration is received in foreign exchange or settled through cross-border payment channels; and (4) the enterprise maintains contractual documentation proving the service is exported. The specific regime is the 'VAT zero-rated cross-border services' catalogue under Caishui [2016] No. 36 and supplementary STA announcements. For digital content delivered via online application stores (Apple App Store and Google Play), the WFOE must evidence that the app store acts as a distribution platform and that end-user consumers are located outside mainland China; for the offline export of physical comic books or promotional materials, zero-rating requires physical goods to leave China through customs.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or Air Waybill
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) / Foreign Exchange Receipt Voucher or bank SWIFT credit confirmation evidencing cross-border consideration
Export contract or service agreement with the overseas counterparty
VAT special invoice or general invoice for export sales (digital e-invoice) cross-referenced to the export declaration
Digital service delivery log or download/access records evidencing overseas consumption for zero-rated digital services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The State Taxation Administration and the General Administration of Customs jointly scrutinize export zero-rating claims through the Golden Tax System and the China International Trade Single Window data matching engine. Penalties for fraudulent or unsubstantiated export zero-rating include: (1) forced reversal of the zero-rated treatment and retroactive collection of the applicable VAT rate (13% or 9% depending on service classification) plus late surcharge; (2) administrative penalties of 50% to 500% of the unlawfully obtained tax credit or refund under the Law on the Administration of Tax Collection and the VAT implementing rules; (3) forfeiture of the VAT refund or input credit claimed; (4) inclusion in the tax violation blacklist with enhanced supervision and reduced tax credit rating; and (5) criminal liability for fraudulent export tax refund crimes under Article 204 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China, which imposes imprisonment and fines where the defrauded refund amount exceeds the criminal threshold. Foreign exchange repatriation beyond the 180-day statutory deadline without an approved extension causes the export proceeds verification records to be marked non-performing, leading to mandatory VAT reversal and penalties under the foreign exchange administration rules.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) under the People's Bank of China (PBOC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China's FX regulatory framework divides the current account and capital account. Payments for digital content licensing, webtoon subscription settlements, and related service trade fees are classified as current account transactions and are freely convertible once genuine transaction documents are presented and verified by a designated bank. Profit remittance by the WFOE to its Taiwan shareholder is permitted as current account profit remittance after statutory annual audit, corporate income tax filing, avoidance of double taxation verification, and a FIE profit distribution resolution; SAFE and the remitting bank will require proof of audited financials, tax clearance, board resolution, and prior capital verification. Capital account transactions including equity investment, shareholder loans, and liquidation proceeds remain subject to pre-registration with SAFE, bank quotas, and strict use restrictions. No general convertibility right exists for capital account items; each transaction requires a legal basis or regulatory approval.

stage_4.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under SAFE rules (Circular 2019/28 and related implementing regulations), export and service trade proceeds received by a domestic entity must be repatriated into China within 180 days of the date of settlement performance or customs declaration, whichever is applicable. For webtoon licensing and digital syndication revenues, verification is based on the underlying service contract and the actual service performance date; no fixed percentage must be forcibly converted into RMB, and the enterprise may retain proceeds in a foreign currency settlement account or convert into RMB at its discretion. However, every settlement through the banking channel must satisfy genuineness and consistency review by the designated bank; retained foreign exchange balances remain subject to reinvestment and account balance monitoring.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Shareholders' Meeting Resolutions and Audited Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commerce
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of fiscal year-end; for a December 31 year-end, no later than June 30 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of NT$10,000–NT$150,000 against the responsible director; repeat non-compliance may lead to involuntary company dissolution by the competent authority.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return and Unappropriated Earnings Allocation Statement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by May 31 for calendar-year taxpayers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge and interest on underpaid tax; understatement surcharge of up to three times the tax evaded; criminal investigation applicable for willful evasion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before April 30 of each year following the reporting fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file may result in revocation or suspension of the foreign investment approval; no separate monetary fine is prescribed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Registration Records Refresh and Substantial Shareholder Register Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Taiwan Company Registration System / Competent Authority via Corporate Affairs Business Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within fifteen days after the annual shareholders' meeting approving financial statements; compelled as a continuing registration obligation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty per Company Act for failing to update registration; subsequent transactions may be deemed prejudicial to third parties; repeated infractions may trigger a compulsory deregistration procedure.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent CPA audit is mandatory for public companies and for any Taiwan company whose paid-in capital exceeds NT$30 million (approximately USD 1,000,000), or whose annual revenue exceeds NT$100 million; otherwise a voluntary review or compilation is permitted.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as endorsed by the Financial Supervisory Commission for public companies; non-public companies may apply Taiwan GAAP (IFRS-aligned) or the IFRS for SMEs equivalently accepted by the Ministry of Finance.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Taiwan Company Act and AML framework, each company must maintain an up-to-date substantial shareholder register (shareholders holding 5% or more of the issued shares). No standalone annual UBO filing is required; however, at the annual shareholders' meeting the directors must confirm the register is current, and any share transfers during the year must be registered with the Corporate Affairs Business Office within thirty days. Failure to maintain the register may expose the responsible person to criminal or administrative penalties.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 – USD 15,000 for a non-public WFOE of comparable scale

jurisdictional_scope_and_qualification.jurisdiction_basis: The payload identifies Taiwan as jurisdiction_id TW. Taiwan tax rules are therefore applied to the local entity and Taiwan-source income.
jurisdictional_scope_and_qualification.entity_classification_assumption: Taiwan-incorporated limited company or Taiwan permanent establishment operated under the supplied WFOE label.
jurisdictional_scope_and_qualification.mainland_china_caveat: A mainland China wholly foreign-owned enterprise is governed by mainland China tax law, not Taiwan tax law. The entity registration location must be confirmed before filing.
jurisdictional_scope_and_qualification.tax_loss_schema_correction: The supplied mandatory value of 5 years conflicts with Taiwan law. Taiwan generally permits qualifying business losses to be carried forward for 10 years, subject to statutory bookkeeping, blue-return or tax-certification requirements and timely filing.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 20% corporate income tax on taxable business income
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying technology, innovation, cultural-content, startup and investment projects may receive statutory tax credits, accelerated deductions or investment incentives. Eligibility is activity-specific and generally requires prior approval, certification or compliance with prescribed conditions. No automatic reduced rate applies solely to digital webtoon publishing or comic syndication.
corporate_income_tax_regime.loss_carryforward_conditions: Losses are generally available for 10 years only where the company maintains required accounting books, files returns within the statutory period and satisfies applicable tax-audit or blue-return conditions. Losses may be restricted by ownership changes, reorganizations, cessation of business or anti-avoidance rules.
corporate_income_tax_regime.minimum_tax: Taiwan alternative minimum tax may apply to companies with specified tax-exempt income, qualifying securities transactions or other add-back items. The corporate alternative minimum tax rate is generally 12% on adjusted basic income above the statutory threshold.
corporate_income_tax_regime.business_tax: Taiwan business tax is generally 5% for ordinary VAT-taxable supplies. Digital content, platform access, licensing and cross-border electronic services require transaction-by-transaction classification.
corporate_income_tax_regime.taxable_income_basis: Taxable income is based on accounting profit adjusted for non-deductible expenses, exempt income, tax credits, depreciation differences, related-party adjustments and other provisions of the Income Tax Act.
corporate_income_tax_regime.fiscal_year: The standard fiscal year is the calendar year unless an approved alternative fiscal year applies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return; electronically filed through the Taiwan Ministry of Finance e-Filing or tax-agent filing system, with supporting schedules submitted in prescribed electronic formats where applicable.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar-year company, file and pay by 31 May of the following year. Companies using an approved non-calendar fiscal year generally file within five months after fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company uniform business number, legal name, registered address, responsible person, fiscal year and tax office jurisdiction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident company files only where it has Taiwan-source income or a Taiwan permanent establishment. Use the Taiwan tax identification number if registered; otherwise apply the non-resident filing procedure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total revenue from webtoon subscriptions, chapter unlocking, digital downloads, advertising, syndication, licensing, commissions and other operating activities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate Taiwan-source revenue using the place of performance, customer location, exploitation location, payment obligations and applicable source rules. Do not treat foreign-platform settlement location as conclusive.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Cost of goods sold and direct content costs
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Creator royalties, translation costs, editorial production, platform commissions, payment-processing costs and other directly attributable costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Retain enforceable contracts, royalty statements, invoices, withholding evidence and allocation schedules. Payments to foreign creators may require Taiwan withholding analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Payroll, marketing, cloud hosting, software, legal, accounting, office, depreciation and other ordinary and necessary business expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductibility requires business purpose, documentary evidence and arm's-length support. Foreign expenses should be supported by contracts, invoices, payment records and translation where requested.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest, foreign-exchange gains or losses, investment income, disposal gains, penalties and other non-operating items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Classify Taiwan-source interest and investment income separately because withholding tax, gross-basis taxation or treaty relief may apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transactions with foreign parent companies, affiliates, platform entities, licensors, service companies and common-control parties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose controlled transactions by type and counterparty jurisdiction. Reconcile return amounts to the transfer-pricing report, general ledger and intercompany invoices.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible expenses, provisions, entertainment limits, depreciation differences, exempt income, tax incentives and transfer-pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply Taiwan tax adjustments even where the foreign parent uses different accounting standards. Maintain a book-to-tax reconciliation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Current-year loss, prior-year loss carryforward and loss utilized in the year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use losses only when statutory filing, accounting and documentation conditions are met. Retain schedules proving the origin, age and utilization of each loss.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Taxable income and corporate income tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income multiplied by the applicable 20% rate, reduced by valid tax credits and increased by applicable alternative minimum tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident without a permanent establishment may be taxed by withholding or assessment on gross Taiwan-source amounts rather than through ordinary net-income filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provisional tax, withholding credits, foreign tax credits, installments, balance payable and refund claim.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile every credit to an official withholding certificate or payment record. Foreign tax credits require statutory limitations and supporting foreign tax evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Certification by the responsible person and, where applicable, the appointed tax agent or authorized representative.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure the responsible person has authority under corporate records and that electronic credentials, power of attorney and tax-agent appointments remain valid.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing generally triggers a surcharge based on assessed tax, commonly 10% subject to statutory minimums and maximums. Failure to file may result in assessment by the tax authority, loss of loss carryforwards, additional late-payment interest and collection measures. Late payment generally incurs a 1% surcharge for each period of delay within the statutory cap, plus interest. Exact amounts depend on the Income Tax Act, Tax Collection Act and the assessment date.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Provisional Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return; electronically filed through the Ministry of Finance system.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally filed from 1 September through 30 September for the first six months of the calendar year, unless the company uses an approved alternative fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Prior-year tax basis or current-period accounting basis
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax calculated using the prior year's assessed tax or the first-half current-year taxable result, as permitted.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the method legally available to the taxpayer and maintain reconciliation to the final annual return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interim corporate income tax payment credited against the annual liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not treat provisional payment as final tax. Reconcile it to the annual return and retain payment confirmation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file or pay may generate surcharge, interest and collection action. Excess provisional tax is generally creditable against the final annual liability but is not automatically refundable without the applicable annual assessment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Business Tax Return, typically filed on the VAT cycle through the Taiwan electronic business-tax filing system.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally file and pay by the 15th day of the month following the end of each two-month VAT period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taiwan VAT-taxable sales, including qualifying digital content and services supplied in Taiwan.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Determine whether the customer, consumption, performance or exploitation location creates Taiwan VAT. Foreign platform processing does not automatically eliminate Taiwan VAT.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Sales qualifying for zero rating or exemption under Taiwan business-tax rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use zero-rating only with required export or cross-border evidence. Exempt and zero-rated treatment have different input-tax consequences.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Recoverable VAT supported by valid invoices and eligible import or expense documents.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign invoices generally do not constitute Taiwan input-tax credits without the required import or local tax documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Output VAT less allowable input VAT.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the return to platform statements, payment processors, sales ledgers and customer-location evidence.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing, non-filing, under-reporting and fraudulent invoice use may result in fixed penalties, tax assessment, additional business tax, interest and, for serious cases, criminal liability. The statutory result depends on the type and duration of violation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Withholding tax return and withholding certificates; electronically filed through the Taiwan withholding-tax system.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Generally monthly or upon the statutory payment deadline, with annual reporting and certificate obligations for specified payments.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Tax withheld from payments is generally remitted by the 10th day of the following month, subject to special rules for dividends, salaries and other payment categories.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Recipient name, tax number, address, residence status, beneficial-owner status and payment category.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Obtain a foreign recipient's tax residency certificate and beneficial-owner information before applying treaty relief.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross dividend, interest, royalty, service fee, commission or other Taiwan-source payment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not net foreign taxes, bank charges or platform fees unless legally permitted and documented.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Domestic statutory rate or approved treaty rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the statutory rate unless treaty relief has been properly supported and accepted by the competent authority.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax withheld, remittance date, certificate number and recipient reporting details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Issue the required certificate and retain proof of remittance and delivery to the recipient.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to withhold, under-withholding, late remittance or failure to issue certificates may result in recovery of the unpaid tax from the withholding agent, penalties, interest and possible director or responsible-person liability in cases involving intentional concealment or fraud.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 21% on dividends paid by a Taiwan company to a non-resident company or non-resident individual, subject to applicable treaty or special statutory relief.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Taiwan has an income-tax treaty network, but there is no comprehensive Taiwan-mainland China double-tax treaty equivalent to an ordinary bilateral DTA. Treaty relief requires a treaty with the recipient's jurisdiction, proof of tax residence, beneficial ownership and satisfaction of anti-abuse conditions. The payer should obtain a current tax residency certificate, payment agreement, ownership chain and substance evidence. Where advance approval is required, apply to the competent Taiwan tax authority before payment or before filing the withholding return. Otherwise withhold at the domestic rate and pursue refund or adjustment under the applicable administrative procedure.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid to a non-resident are generally subject to 20% withholding. Interest paid to a non-resident is generally subject to 20% withholding, with special rates potentially applying to specified bonds, government instruments, securitized products or approved financial transactions. Treaty rates vary by recipient jurisdiction and commonly reduce royalties and interest below 20%, subject to the applicable treaty, residence certificate, beneficial ownership, limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose requirements.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.service_fee_caveat: Payments characterized as technical, management, advertising, platform, commission or digital services may be Taiwan-source income if services are performed in Taiwan or otherwise meet Taiwan source rules. Classification must not be used to avoid royalty or service withholding.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.repatriation_controls: Dividends may generally be remitted after approval of financial statements, allocation of earnings and satisfaction of capital impairment and corporate-law requirements. Banks may require corporate resolutions, tax clearance or withholding evidence, audited financial statements and foreign-exchange documentation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.foreign_exchange_and_banking: Cross-border remittance must comply with Taiwan foreign-exchange reporting and banking due-diligence requirements. Suspicious payment chains, unexplained shareholder loans and circular fund flows may trigger enhanced AML review.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File: generally required where annual net sales and non-operating income reach at least NT$300 million or the aggregate amount of controlled transactions reaches at least NT$200 million, subject to statutory exemptions and transaction-specific rules. Master File: generally required for a Taiwan constituent entity of an MNE group where consolidated group revenue reaches at least NT$3 billion. Country-by-Country Reporting generally applies at the group threshold of approximately NT$27 billion or the equivalent EUR 750 million threshold, subject to current Taiwan rules.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Other OECD-consistent methods where the prescribed methods cannot reasonably be applied
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Taiwan does not operate a single broad offshore Economic Substance Regulation regime equivalent to certain low-tax jurisdictions. Substance is nevertheless relevant under transfer-pricing rules, the general anti-avoidance rule, beneficial-owner analysis, controlled foreign company rules, treaty anti-abuse standards and source-of-income rules. The company should maintain Taiwan personnel, decision-making records, premises or operational infrastructure, IP and licensing control, risk assumption, customer and platform functions and commercially credible accounting records consistent with the claimed profit allocation.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.controlled_transaction_scope: Controlled transactions include purchases, sales, services, royalties, financing, guarantees, leases, cost sharing, restructuring and transfers of intangible property with related parties or entities under common control.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.annual_compliance: Prepare a related-party transaction disclosure, intercompany reconciliation, functional analysis, benchmarking support and Local File or Master File where thresholds are met. Documentation should be available by the filing deadline and retained for the statutory audit period.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.webtoon_specific_tp_risks: Allocate profit among IP ownership, adaptation rights, translation, editorial control, platform operation, customer acquisition, payment processing, content moderation and local market exploitation. A routine distributor return is inappropriate if the Taiwan entity controls valuable local marketing intangibles, bears platform or regulatory risks, or performs substantial content exploitation functions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.deduction_risk: Royalties, management fees, platform fees and regional service charges require benefit evidence, pricing support, withholding compliance and proof that the Taiwan entity actually received the stated service.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.customs_and_tax_consistency: Although digital content may not involve customs entries, intercompany revenue, royalty, service and financing classifications must be consistent across tax returns, accounting records, withholding filings, VAT records, transfer-pricing reports and bank documentation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and false tax reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing Taiwan-source revenue, creating false expenses, omitting platform receipts, using fabricated invoices, manipulating revenue recognition or knowingly filing materially false income-tax or VAT returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax assessment, recovery of unpaid tax, statutory surcharges, interest and criminal prosecution. Intentional evasion may result in imprisonment of up to five years and a criminal fine of up to NT$10 million under the Tax Collection Act, subject to the specific offense and court determination.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The company is ordinarily a separate legal person, but the responsible person, director, manager, accountant or other participant may face criminal prosecution, civil restitution, tax recovery, asset preservation and restrictions on departure from Taiwan for serious tax arrears or statutory violations. The corporate veil is not routinely pierced solely because tax is unpaid.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing or receiving accommodation invoices, claiming input tax without genuine transactions, using third-party invoices to inflate deductions or operating an undisclosed sales channel.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Rejection of input credits, additional business tax, statutory fines that may be multiple times the improperly claimed or evaded tax, interest and criminal sanctions for aggravated fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible persons and participating officers may incur criminal liability, joint tax recovery, civil damages and restrictions on departure where statutory conditions are met.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to withhold or remit tax on dividends, royalties, interest, service fees or other Taiwan-source payments, or applying treaty rates without supporting residence and beneficial-owner documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The withholding agent may be assessed for the unpaid tax, interest, penalties and certificate-related fines. Treaty relief may be denied and the payer may become liable for the shortfall.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and responsible persons may be pursued where they authorized or knowingly participated in non-withholding, concealment or fraudulent documentation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Excessive offshore royalties, artificial management fees, non-arm's-length platform charges, debt loading, loss allocation inconsistent with functions or failure to disclose related-party transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax authority adjustment to taxable income, denial of deductions, deemed income or deemed interest, withholding reassessment, interest, penalties and documentation-related sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors generally face corporate rather than automatic personal liability, but may be liable for intentional fraud, breach of fiduciary duty, unlawful distributions or participation in tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company and lack of economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a nominal Taiwan company with no personnel, functions, decision-making, assets or commercial risk while booking substantial profits or claiming treaty, deduction or source-of-income benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, reallocation of income, disallowance of expenses, permanent-establishment or Taiwan-source income assessment, interest, penalties and possible anti-avoidance adjustment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible persons may face civil claims, tax recovery and criminal liability if sham arrangements, false records or fraudulent declarations are used. A mere low-substance profile is not automatically criminal but is a severe audit indicator.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlawful profit distribution and capital impairment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends without distributable earnings, ignoring statutory loss coverage, making shareholder loans disguised as dividends or remitting funds before corporate approvals and tax compliance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Invalid or challengeable distribution, repayment obligation, director liability for damages, shareholder repayment exposure and possible corporate-law fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly liable for restitution and damages caused by unlawful distributions. Criminal liability may arise where false accounts, fraud or breach of trust is established.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML, sanctions and suspicious payment activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Circular payments, unexplained payments to creators or licensors, nominee shareholders, rapid movement through unrelated jurisdictions, false payment descriptions or transactions involving sanctioned persons.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Account freezing, transaction rejection, regulatory reporting, administrative fines and criminal prosecution under Taiwan AML and related laws. Serious money-laundering offenses may carry substantial imprisonment and fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, officers and beneficial owners who direct, facilitate or knowingly ignore laundering activity may face criminal imprisonment, fines, confiscation, civil restitution and travel restrictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Syndicating webtoons without valid assignment, translation, adaptation, territorial, platform or derivative-work rights, or using unlicensed music, images, fonts or AI-generated material.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil injunctions, damages, disgorgement, destruction of infringing materials and potential criminal copyright penalties. Unlicensed royalties may also create tax deduction and withholding disputes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and managers may face personal liability where they knowingly authorize infringement, participate in commercial exploitation or abuse the corporate form to evade judgments.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Unlawful collection of subscriber data, failure to provide required consumer disclosures, misleading subscription or auto-renewal terms, or inadequate cross-border transfer safeguards.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines, corrective orders, service restrictions, consumer refunds and civil damages under applicable Taiwan data-protection and consumer-protection laws.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability depends on the applicable statute, knowledge, authorization and degree of participation. Directors may face damages claims for negligent governance or failure to implement required controls.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a mainland China WFOE registration, tax number or bank account while filing as a Taiwan company, or treating Taiwan operations as outside the registered entity's tax jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Invalid filings, missed tax registrations, dual-jurisdiction assessments, penalties, withholding failures, foreign-exchange issues and possible licensing or investment-compliance consequences.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible persons may face administrative sanctions, tax recovery, civil liability and criminal exposure where the misclassification involves intentional concealment or false declarations.

critical_action_items: Confirm whether the legal entity is incorporated in Taiwan or mainland China before applying any tax rate, filing deadline or withholding rule.
Map all revenue streams by customer location, platform, payment flow, IP right and place of performance.
Prepare a Taiwan-source income and VAT position paper for subscriptions, chapter unlocking, advertising, licensing and syndication.
Obtain residency certificates and beneficial-owner evidence before applying any treaty withholding rate.
Document IP ownership, creator contracts, translation rights, territorial rights and platform exploitation rights.
Perform a related-party transaction inventory and test the NT$300 million, NT$200 million and NT$3 billion documentation thresholds.
Reconcile accounting records, platform statements, VAT filings, withholding returns, corporate income-tax filings and bank receipts.
Establish a dividend approval and remittance checklist covering distributable earnings, tax withholding, corporate approvals and foreign-exchange documentation.
Maintain substance evidence for personnel, decision-making, functions, assets, risks and commercial rationale in Taiwan.

Obtain jurisdiction-specific advice if the entity is actually a mainland China WFOE, because mainland China corporate income tax, VAT, withholding, transfer-pricing and profit-remittance rules would replace the Taiwan analysis.
